title: PipelineK
description: One panel per signal family: what the product measured, the question the measurement answers and the decision it allows.

panels.title: Compile duration (p95)
panels.description: Product's metric: pipelinek.boundary_duration_ms, operation_kind=compile. Question: how long does compiling the script take? Decision: a compile that grows is the pipeline's own cost, so the fix is in the script.

panels.title: Step duration (p95)
panels.description: Product's metric: pipelinek.boundary_duration_ms, operation_kind=step.dispatch. Question: how long does a dispatched step take? Decision: the step that dominates the run is the one to parallelise, cache or move to a faster runner.

panels.title: Queue and provisioning (p95)
panels.description: Product's metric: pipelinek.boundary_duration_ms, operation_kind=step.preparation. Question: how long did a step wait before it was allowed to run? Decision: this time is the cost of admission and of the wait, not the step's own time.

panels.title: Recovery duration (p95)
panels.description: Product's metric: pipelinek.boundary_duration_ms, operation_kind=recovery. Question: how long does recovering an unobserved operation take? Decision: a recovery that grows is a durability problem, and the run's result does not depend on it.

panels.title: Failures by class
panels.description: Product's metric: pipelinek.boundary_total. Question: which failures happened, and of which class? Decision: the class says who has to act, so it is what routes the alert and not the count alone.

panels.title: Telemetry loss
panels.description: Product's metric: pipelinek.export_loss_total. Question: did the telemetry itself fail to leave the process? Decision: a growing loss means the picture is incomplete; the run's own result does not change, so this is a question about trust.
